svg.aria-label: How to write о: one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
svg.title: Writing о
svg.desc: 2 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of о (cyrillic), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase о demonstration, 05:59–06:03, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source note on variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 05:59–06:03 lowercase о demonstration, the pen begins at the upper right, curves left across the top, descends the left side, sweeps through the bottom, rises along the right side, and closes the oval at its starting point in one continuous counterclockwise pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a tall, slightly slanted oval; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a wider, upright printed oval. This learner path preserves the source's upper-right-to-left-side-to-bottom-to-right-side closure order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline as one closed counterclockwise oval. Connected cursive may add entry and exit joins to the source's clean isolated closure, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the oval differently.
